title: International Typographic Style
summary: Grids, sans-serif type, and objective images. Order as the message.
lede: A modernist graphic design approach, formalized in Switzerland in the 1950s, that builds every layout on a modular grid, sets flush-left sans-serif type, and prefers objective photography to illustration.

era.note: Roots in the 1920s New Typography. Wikipedia dates its emergence to the 1930s–1950s.

lineage.label: New Typography
lineage.note: Jan Tschichold’s 1928 book *Die neue Typographie* argued for asymmetric layouts and sans-serif type. Wikipedia describes the style as formalizing these 1920s innovations.
Bauhaus typography and teaching preceded the style. Max Bill studied at the Bauhaus and later co-founded the Ulm School of Design.
Both put structure first and remove decoration. Minimalist Machine adds monospaced, technical labels.

grammar.text: Columns and rows set every position and every image size. The grid is often visible through alignment alone.
Akzidenz-Grotesk, Helvetica, and Univers in a small number of sizes and weights. Text is flush left and ragged right.
Content hangs from a strong axis. Large empty areas are part of the composition, not leftover space.
One very large element, such as a headline or number, against small, even body text.
Black and white with one or two flat colors, often red. No gradients.
Black-and-white photography and simple geometric forms instead of illustration.

diagnostic: Most elements align to a consistent column grid.
Headings and body use a grotesque or neo-grotesque sans-serif.
Text is flush left and ragged right. Centered text is rare.
Color is flat and limited to two or three hues plus black and white.
counter: Decorative or script typefaces carry the message.
Gradients, glossy surfaces, textures, or drop shadows are important to the look.
Illustration with a hand-drawn character is the main image type.

confusions.difference: Minimalist Machine uses monospaced labels, outlined boxes, and visible connections. The International Typographic Style relies on grid and type scale alone.
Minimal sites are often centered, with one column and soft gray type. This style is asymmetric, with a strong grid and strong scale contrast.

do: Build the page on a 12-column grid and align every block to column edges.
Use one grotesque family in two weights. Set body text flush left.
Make one element very large, for example the headline or a date, and keep the rest small.
Use black, white, and one accent color. Use the accent for one idea per view.
Keep generous empty space around groups.
dont: Do not center headings and paragraphs by default.
Do not add rounded corners, drop shadows, or gradients.
Do not use more than two type sizes for body content.
Do not fill empty grid areas with decoration.
avoid: Brands that sell luxury, romance, or nostalgia. The style holds emotion back.

fingerprint.note: Strong scale contrast between display and body.
At most one accent hue, usually red.
Grotesque sans-serif throughout. Monospaced text points to Minimalist Machine.

synthesis: The type came first. [Akzidenz-Grotesk](ref:akzidenz-grotesk-typeface), [Helvetica](ref:helvetica-typeface), and [Univers](ref:univers-typeface) supplied the neutral grotesques that the posters and books depend on.

Posters such as [Der Film](ref:der-film-poster-1960) and [Giselle](ref:giselle-poster-1959) show the method at full scale: one strong axis, flush-left type, and black-and-white photography with a single red.

The method spread through print: the journal [Neue Grafik](ref:neue-grafik-journal-1958-1965), Emil Ruder’s [Typographie](ref:typographie-emil-ruder-1967), Karl Gerstner’s [Capital grid](ref:capital-magazine-layout-grid-gerstner), and Müller-Brockmann’s [Grid Systems](ref:grid-systems-in-graphic-design-1981).

Systems for public space carry it into three dimensions: the [NYCTA graphics standards](ref:nycta-graphics-standards-manual-1970) and the [Munich 1972 pictograms](ref:munich-1972-olympic-pictograms). This is the line that leads to interface design systems.

On the web the style lives on at cultural institutions and design studios. The [Stedelijk](ref:stedelijk-website) and [Whitney](ref:whitney-website) home pages, the [ZHdK](ref:zhdk-website) site, and the [Experimental Jetset](ref:jetset-website) archive are clear examples captured on 25 September 2026. [MoMA](ref:moma-website) uses the type without a visible grid and adds a second accent, and [The Swiss Grid](ref:swiss-grid-poster-house-website) exhibition site centers its title block.

Captures tested the fingerprint. Stedelijk and Whitney pass every metric. Experimental Jetset and ZHdK fail `type.sizeRange` for two different reasons: Jetset sets every line at one size, and on ZHdK large links hold most of the characters, so the base size is 45 px. The range is unchanged until more clear examples fail it. `type.centerShare` measures text alignment only. It does not see a left-aligned block that margins center, as on The Swiss Grid, so judge centering from the screenshot.
